title: M1A Mains · Paper I · Section A · Social and Cultural History of Andhra Pradesh (75M) › M1A.2 Andhradesa, 11th to 16th centuries A.D.

syllabus_leaves.wording: Various Major and minor dynasties that ruled Andhradesa between 11th and 16th centuries A.D
Socio-Religious and Economic Conditions, Growth of Telugu Language and Literature, Art and Architecture in Andhradesa between 11th to 16th centuries A.D
Growth of Telugu language and literature

official_questions.stem: The remains of the Vijayanagar empire can be found in
official_questions.core_fact: The ruins of Vijayanagara, the capital of the Vijayanagara empire, are at Hampi (Karnataka; UNESCO WHS 1986).

statements.t: The remains of the Vijayanagar empire can be found at Bijapur.
statements.fact: Bijapur was the Adil Shahi capital.

official_questions.rule: Vijayanagara capital = Hampi; Bahmani successors: Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmadnagar, Bidar, Berar.

official_questions.stem: The popular name of Ramachandra temple at Hampi is
official_questions.core_fact: The Ramachandra temple in Hampi's royal centre (royal chapel, Krishnadevaraya era) is popularly called the Hazara Rama temple (friezes of the Ramayana).

statements.t: The popular name of the Ramachandra temple at Hampi is the Vitthala temple.

official_questions.rule: Hampi: Virupaksha (oldest), Vitthala (stone chariot), Hazara Rama (royal chapel), Krishna (1513).

official_questions.stem: Commentaries on Vedas were written under the leadership of Sayana and Madhava during the period of
official_questions.core_fact: Sayana and Madhava (Vidyaranya) wrote Vedic commentaries (Vedartha Prakasha) under the early Sangamas - begun under Bukka I and continued under Harihara II, whose minister Sayana was.

statements.t: The Vedic commentaries of Sayana and Madhava were written during the period of Bukka I.
The Vedic commentaries of Sayana and Madhava were written during the period of Devaraya I.

statements.t: The Vedic commentaries of Sayana and Madhava were written during the period of Harihara II.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked

statements.t: The Vedic commentaries of Sayana and Madhava were written during the period of Harihara I.

official_questions.rule: Sangama: Harihara I & Bukka I (founders, Vidyaranya), Harihara II (Sayana minister), Devaraya I/II.

official_questions.stem: The Kakatiya king who shifted the capital from Anumakonda to Warangal was
official_questions.core_fact: Ganapatideva (1199-1262) completed Orugallu (Warangal) and shifted the capital from Anumakonda (Hanumakonda).

statements.t: The Kakatiya king who shifted the capital from Anumakonda to Warangal was Rudradeva.

official_questions.rule: Kakatiya capital: Anumakonda -> Orugallu under Ganapatideva.

official_questions.stem: Nritta Ratnavali was composed by Jayapa in
official_questions.core_fact: Jayapa Senani, Ganapatideva's elephant commander, wrote the dance treatise Nritta Ratnavali in Sanskrit.

official_questions.rule: Kakatiya sastra: Nritta Ratnavali (Sanskrit, Jayapa); Pratapa Rudriyam (Sanskrit, Vidyanatha).

official_questions.stem: The most favoured musical instrument of Vijayanagar period was
official_questions.core_fact: The veena was the most favoured instrument at the Vijayanagara court (Krishnadevaraya and Ramaraya era patronage of Carnatic music).

statements.t: The most favoured musical instrument of the Vijayanagar period was the Tabla.

statements.t: The most favoured musical instrument of the Vijayanagar period was the Flute.

official_questions.rule: Vijayanagara music: veena; Purandaradasa - father of Carnatic music.

official_questions.stem: Who described the physical features of Krishnadevaraya in detail ?
official_questions.core_fact: Portuguese Domingo Paes (c. 1520-22) described Krishnadevaraya's physical features in detail; Fernao Nuniz wrote a chronicle of the kings.

statements.t: Peddanna described the physical features of Krishnadevaraya in detail.

Nuniz described the physical features of Krishnadevaraya in detail.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: Nuniz wrote the dynastic chronicle; Paes described the king.

official_questions.rule: Paes (1520-22) - king's appearance, city; Nuniz (1535-37) - history; Abdur Razzaq (1443) - Devaraya II.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following structures is mentioned as an example of Indo-Sarcenic art by Longhurst ?
official_questions.core_fact: A.H. Longhurst ('Hampi Ruins', 1917) cited the Padma (Lotus) Mahal in the Zenana enclosure as an Indo-Saracenic example (Islamic arches on Hindu base).

statements.t: Longhurst mentions the Bhuvana Vijayam as an example of Indo-Saracenic art.

statements.fact: Bhuvana Vijayam was the literary assembly hall.

statements.t: Longhurst mentions the Elephants stables as an example of Indo-Saracenic art.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: Elephant stables are Indo-Islamic too, but the key example is the Padma Mahal.

official_questions.rule: Hampi Indo-Islamic: Lotus Mahal, Elephant Stables, Queen's Bath.

official_questions.stem: Identity the lake which is mentioned in the Pithapuram inscription of Prithvisvara of Velanadu
official_questions.core_fact: The Pithapuram inscription of the Velanati chief Prithvisvara mentions Kolleru lake (between Krishna and Godavari deltas).

official_questions.rule: Kolleru = coastal Andhra lake in medieval records (Velanati, Kolleru island fort).

official_questions.stem: The Raichur Doab is formed by the Confluence of Rivers
official_questions.core_fact: The Raichur Doab lies between the Krishna (north) and the Tungabhadra (south).

statements.t: The Raichur Doab is formed by the rivers Krishna and Tungabhadra.

official_questions.rule: Raichur Doab = Krishna-Tungabhadra; contested by Vijayanagara and Bahmanis.

official_questions.stem: Which inscription mentioned about Kakatiyas for the first time

official_questions.stem: Kakatiyas were subordinates of which dynasty in Andhra
official_questions.core_fact: The early Kakatiyas were feudatories of the Rashtrakutas (later of the Kalyani Chalukyas).

official_questions.rule: Kakatiya overlords: Rashtrakutas -> Kalyani Chalukyas -> independence (Rudradeva).

official_questions.stem: Which of the following defeated Ganapatideva in 1263

official_questions.stem: During the ancient and medieval days, Pradvivaka was an adviser to the king in:

official_questions.stem: Surambika, the queen of Pedakomativema excavated a tank known as:
